methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU's partnership with AI Ready RVA signals intentional community-driven AI capability building beyond elite institutions, potentially distributing deep literacy through Richmond's civic infrastructure if sustained beyond programmatic announcement.

signals.title: EPA grant backs community-driven workforce training in Southwest Virginia - Virginia Tech News
signals.signal_reading: EPA-funded community-driven workforce training in Southwest Virginia represents rare distributed capacity investment in transitioning economy, testing whether peer networks can build deep AI fluency outside metro gravity wells.

signals.title: AI bills faced a logjam in the General Assembly due to a Trump executive order, but Congress is working to fill the gap
signals.signal_reading: Federal pressure blocking state AI legislation prevents Virginia from building regulatory capacity or workforce frameworks, risking neither depth nor distribution as policy vacuum leaves regions dependent on federal broadband funds without local adaptation mechanisms.

signals.title: AI pressure grows on Richmond's young workforce - Axios
signals.signal_reading: AI pressure on Richmond's young workforce signals concentrated capability demands in metro hub without evidence of distributed skilling infrastructure, reinforcing geographic sorting of talent toward existing centers.

signals.title: Why more residents are saying ‘No’ to AI data centers in their backyard - NPR
signals.signal_reading: NoVA resident resistance to AI data centers reveals concentration tensions where infrastructure density creates backlash, potentially limiting even hub expansion while rural areas compete for economic development—neither distributing capability nor deepening community buy-in.
